item.title: Just Show Up
item.dc:creator: Brainard Carey
item.description: At times it can feel like everyone else is getting the exhibition, the grant, the residency, or the attention you’ve been working toward. Building an art career is rarely a straight line, rather it’s a process of showing up, continuing to make work that matters to you, and staying connected to opportunities that can move […]
item.content:encoded:
At times it can feel like everyone else is getting the exhibition, the grant, the residency, or the attention you’ve been working toward. Building an art career is rarely a straight line, rather it’s a process of showing up, continuing to make work that matters to you, and staying connected to opportunities that can move your practice forward. Every application you submit, every new resource you discover, and every connection you make adds another piece to the foundation you’re building.

The Blu Sky Artist Award offers more than cash prizes, providing two winners and 20 finalists with editorial features, collector exposure, career-building recognition, and lasting visibility for their work. Learn more at the website. Deadline is August 15.

Compete for an AUD$80,000 prize pool in the Head On Photo Awards, open worldwide to photographers of all levels. Anonymous judging, prestigious exhibitions, and international exposure await standout images. For more information and to submit your work, visit the website. Deadline is August 16.

Prospect Art seeks global visual artists for its 2027 NEW WORK commission, awarding $1,500 for conceptually driven projects exploring We Come in Pieces. One application also qualifies artists for ONE WORK and BROADCAST opportunities. Visit the website for more details. Deadline is August 16.

Praxis Center gets it. We really do. The road can feel long and hard – impossible at times. Keep going. There are more paths into the art world than ever before, and with the right information and a little persistence, the next opportunity could be the one that changes everything.

 

Photo credit: Blu Sky Artist Award

item.title: It All Fades Eventually
item.dc:creator: Brainard Carey
item.description: “All things, my son, transmute into old age, life diminishes, everything declines, the proliferation of kinds is a mere illusion, and no one knows to what end.” W.G. Sebald, After Nature Perhaps this quote from Sebald offers little reassurance, instead reminding us that change is relentless, that certainty dissolves, and that much of what we believe […]
item.content:encoded:
“All things, my son, transmute
into old age, life diminishes,
everything declines,
the proliferation
of kinds is a mere
illusion, and no one
knows to what end.”

W.G. Sebald, After Nature

Perhaps this quote from Sebald offers little reassurance, instead reminding us that change is relentless, that certainty dissolves, and that much of what we believe to be permanent is only passing through our hands. And yet, reminders like this can be truly motivating. They can be the catalyst for great things as we come to terms with the temporary nature of everything and everyone around us. Of course, creation cannot stop the world from changing, but it can deepen our encounter with it during the time we have.

Peter Acheson joined us to talk about his show at Anton Kern Gallery, which runs until August 14.The work was created over a number of years, though not intended to be a retrospective. Rather, the work was selected to present a variety of materials and the many facets of Acheson’s process in creating his paintings. To learn more, listen to the complete interview.

Caitlin Keogh spoke with us about her show at Bortolami Gallery, Drawings and Paintings, which runs until August 7. Among the work are floral drawings made during a visit to family in Portland, Oregon where there are public rose gardens. Over the course of her six week visit, she took a chair to the gardens as frequently as she could, focusing on the act of sitting and looking at something right in front of her. To learn more about these works and others in the show, listen to the complete interview.

A Few Words to Keep in Your Pocket.

While it’s true that everything may be in motion, the practice of looking closely remains one of the most enduring forms of hope.

item.title: What Are You Made Of?
item.dc:creator: Brainard Carey
item.description: Every experience, good or bad, large or small, makes you uniquely you. You are the sum of many things, and each and every one of them feeds into your art whether you realize it or not. Of course, most artists can point to the things that inspire them, that feel central to and in their […]
item.content:encoded:
Every experience, good or bad, large or small, makes you uniquely you. You are the sum of many things, and each and every one of them feeds into your art whether you realize it or not. Of course, most artists can point to the things that inspire them, that feel central to and in their work, but what about the more subtle nuances, those currents you may not even realize are moving you – they matter just as much, dare I say it maybe even more. And one of the best ways to keep embracing new experiences is to seek out and apply for as many opportunities as possible. Here are a few to keep you motivated.

Cape Fear Studios invites artists 18+ to submit up to three original works in any medium for its 6 by Exhibit. One dimension must measure 6 inches. Visit the website for more information and to submit work. Deadline is August 10.

Wassaic Project invites artists to submit work, installations, performances, or printed projects for various upcoming deadlines. Learn more at the website. Deadlines vary.

Quinn Emanuel invites Bay Area emerging and mid-career artists to apply for a four-month residency that provides a Silicon Valley studio, $20,000 stipend, $1,500 materials budget, curatorial support, and a culminating exhibition. For details and to apply, visit the website. Deadline is August 14.

Praxis Center believes in the power of artists to shape their lived experience into something worth putting into the world. And we want to ensure each and every one has the resources they need to know how to make that leap. Give Praxis a try today and see how far it can take you.

item.title: What Ails You?
item.dc:creator: Brainard Carey
item.description: “Do you think we ever really survive our childhoods?” Michelle Cunningham, Day Parents often joke that, no matter how much they work to make their children’s upbringing free of events and emotions that may cause them trouble down the road, no one gets out without something to tell a therapist. What if that’s true? What if, […]
item.content:encoded:
“Do you think we ever really survive our childhoods?”

Michelle Cunningham, Day

Parents often joke that, no matter how much they work to make their children’s upbringing free of events and emotions that may cause them trouble down the road, no one gets out without something to tell a therapist. What if that’s true? What if, regardless of how halcyon your youth may have been, all of us carry pieces that could use some reflection? After all, loss is inevitable – whether pets, grandparents, or other loved ones, and parents are only human, flawed in ways perhaps even they can’t see.

Yuya Saito spoke with us recently about Ground Rules, his show on view until July 25 at GOCA by Garde. The body of work on view encompasses a group of sculptures in the style of what Saito terms flow-chitecture, and Park-Scape. Beginning with the city park as a shared public space, Saito’s bent-wood works and new sculptures examine what an open public realm and the idea of freedom can mean today. To learn more, listen to the complete interview.

Kristin Marting joined us in 2021 to discuss her role as the founding artistic director of HERE, the award-winning progressive arts center in lower Manhattan. As communities began emerging from the COVID-19 pandemic, Marting reflected on the unusual experience of spending so much time at home despite being, by nature, a deeply people-oriented theater maker. She also shared the lessons she took from that period, as artists and organizations navigated both the pandemic and a broader national reckoning around racial justice. To hear more about Marting’s work at HERE, her experiences during this transformative time, and her vision for the future of theater, listen to the complete interview.

A Few Words to Keep in Your Pocket.

Have you ever thought back to the things that shaped you and perhaps the things you’d like to process now?

item.title: If It’s Not Comfy, You Should Probably Do It Anyway
item.dc:creator: Brainard Carey
item.description: If you stepped outside your comfort zone more often, could it make a difference in your everyday life? Maybe it means reaching out […]
item.content:encoded:
If you stepped outside your comfort zone more often, could it make a difference in your everyday life? Studies have shown that this can be a powerful way to build resilience and confidence, helping you reach goals you may not otherwise have deemed possible. So, what does that look like? Maybe it means reaching out to a few extra galleries this month, showing up in person to events with strong networking possibilities, or applying for a couple residencies or grants. Whatever stepping out of your usual, safe routine means for you and your career, today might be the day to give it a try.

Stamps Gallery invites Michigan artists and collaboratives to apply for Envision: The Michigan Artist Initiative, celebrating outstanding contemporary art practices and recognizing creativity, innovation, and artistic excellence across the state. Visit the website for more information. Deadline is August 2.

Delaware Division of the Arts Individual Artist Fellowships support creative artists with funding to advance their careers. Administered in partnership with Mid Atlantic Arts, applications are submitted through the Division’s smARTDE system. Learn more at the website. Deadline is August 3.

The Mentor Artist-in-Residence program is a three-week interdisciplinary residency pairing artists with renowned mentors, fostering collaboration, experimentation, critiques, and creative exchange through shared studios and process-based artistic exploration. For more details and to apply, visit the website. Deadline is August 5.

Praxis Center understands the challenges of building a career in the art world. We are here to gently nudge, encourage you to slough off what’s familiar and see how something new might change your outlook – and your path. Why not give Praxis a try today and see how far it can take you.

item.title: Are You Authentic?
item.dc:creator: Brainard Carey
item.description: “Nothing can be truly replicated. Not a love, not a jewel, not a single line.” -Patti Smith, M Train While some things can be copied with remarkable precision, their true essence cannot. A love may be remembered, retold, or even rediscovered, but it is never the same love twice. A jewel may be recut or recreated, […]
item.content:encoded:
“Nothing can be truly replicated. Not a love, not a jewel, not a single line.”

-Patti Smith, M Train

While some things can be copied with remarkable precision, their true essence cannot. A love may be remembered, retold, or even rediscovered, but it is never the same love twice. A jewel may be recut or recreated, but it will never carry the identical history of light, touch, and time. Even a single line of writing exists only in the moment it was conceived, shaped by a unique combination of thought, feeling, and circumstance. Originality is not simply a matter of appearance, rather it is the unrepeatable convergence of experience that gives every creation, every relationship, and every expression its singular value.

Shaun Leonardo spoke to us about his show The Invisible Man, running until August 7 at Christine Tierney Gallery. The title is drawn from the book of the same name as a way to encompass 20 years of work in this survey show. Some works are in direct reference to lines and chapters from the book, while a major throughline is the experience of invisibility as a person of color in the U.S. and the notion that, due to stereotype, there is a subjective version that precedes all people of color into a room. To learn more, listen to the complete interview.

Paco Barragán joined us from Spain in 2022. We spoke with the curator, writer, and critic about his book, his curatorial practice, and the evolving role of the curator. He reflected on the shift from the “total curator”—simultaneously narrator, mythologist, and exhibition designer—to today’s curator as storyteller. Barragán also shared why he believes the traditional “white cube” exhibition model has reached its end. Revisit the full interview to hear his insights on the changing landscape of contemporary curating.

A Few Words to Keep in Your Pocket.

Authenticity remains more enduring than imitation.

item.title: What Keeps You Going?
item.dc:creator: Brainard Carey
item.description: What motivates you to keep moving forward? That could mean moving forward in your pursuit of a career in the art world, or it could mean evolving in pretty much every aspect of your life. If there’s one thing for certain about humans, it’s that we are anything but static. We move through the physical […]
item.content:encoded:
What motivates you to keep moving forward? That could mean moving forward in your pursuit of a career in the art world, or it could mean evolving in pretty much every aspect of your life. If there’s one thing for certain about humans, it’s that we are anything but static. We move through the physical world all the time, but we also move through time and through stages of life. Most of us can reliably say we are not the same people at 40 as we were at 14. So how do you keep up the momentum, find the drive to keep advancing to the next stage? Here are some opportunities to inspire the career side of things.

The Betty Bowen Award honors outstanding Northwest visual artists with a $20,000 unrestricted prize, exhibition at the Seattle Art Museum, and additional recognition awards for exceptional work. Learn more at the website. Deadline is August 1.

Stamps Gallery invites Michigan artists and collaboratives to apply for Envision: The Michigan Artist Initiative, celebrating outstanding contemporary art practices and inspiring future generations through creativity, rigor, and innovation. Visit the website for more information and to apply. Deadline is August 2.

Artists worldwide are invited to apply for the 2026 BigCi Environmental Awards. Two winners receive a four-week residency, A$5,000, research support, and opportunities to explore and present work inspired by UNESCO-listed landscapes. For more details, visit the website. Deadline is August 2.

Praxis Center is dedicated to helping artists achieve the career they’ve always wanted. We can’t make you a professional artist overnight, but we can give you the tools and resources to navigate the art world with confidence and find success. We have seen artist after artist reach heights they never imagined possible. Give Praxis a try today and see how far it can take you.

item.title: You’re In Charge…Aren’t You?
item.dc:creator: Brainard Carey
item.description: “Thought is the original source of all wealth, all success, all material gain, all great discoveries and inventions, and all achievement.” -Claude M. Bristol, The Magic of Believing What do you think of this? Bristol also famously said, “Undoubtedly, we become what we envisage.” Do you agree? Are we capable of manifesting a life with the power […]
item.content:encoded:
“Thought is the original source of all wealth, all success, all material gain, all great discoveries and inventions, and all achievement.”

-Claude M. Bristol, The Magic of Believing

What do you think of this? Bristol also famously said, “Undoubtedly, we become what we envisage.” Do you agree? Are we capable of manifesting a life with the power of thought, or are we simply bumped along by the fates, tossed from the crest of one of life’s waves to the next? Or is it a little of both? Of course, these are questions we will probably never answer for sure, but it is interesting to consider how we all come to the particular circumstances of our lives.

Izzy Barber joined us to discuss her current show, Clay Pigeons, on view at Charles Moffett Gallery until July 31. The work in the show was conceived and created during three separate month-long road trips. Barber would fly to a destination out west and spend time alone there before driving back. While she admits it was not the most financially sustainable practice, it allowed her the needed time to sit with her subjects. To learn more about her process and the work in this show, listen to the complete interview.

Andrej Bereta joined us in 2020 to reflect on his work in Bosnia. He discussed a geography initiative developed in collaboration with the European Union that explores land management and policy through a cultural and curatorial lens. He also shared why he stepped away from traditional curatorial practice to pursue this interdisciplinary work, describing it as an opportunity for change, reflection, and new perspectives. Listen to the full interview to hear more about his experience and the motivations behind this shift.

A Few Words to Keep in Your Pocket.

What do you think? Are we the product of our own mental energy or the victims of the whims of chaos?

item.title: How About A One Stop Shop?
item.dc:creator: Brainard Carey
item.description: Sometimes a single institution offers many opportunities. If you follow this blog regularly, you’ll know that sometimes we focus on one place with many deadlines – think Banff. This week, the spotlight is on Oolite Arts, an artist support organization based in Miami where there are multiple deadlines coming up. Take a look, see if […]
item.content:encoded:
Sometimes a single institution offers many opportunities. If you follow this blog regularly, you’ll know that sometimes we focus on one place with many deadlines – think Banff. This week, the spotlight is on Oolite Arts, an artist support organization based in Miami where there are multiple deadlines coming up. Take a look, see if one of these might be right for you, and if so, put your name in the running. The worst thing they can say is no, and even if they to, there’s always next time.

Oolite Arts’ Home + Away Residency offers paid, multi-week residencies with studio time, professional networking, and community building at partner institutions including Bag Factory, Artpace San Antonio, and MASS MoCA. Visit the website for more info. Deadline is July 31.

The Oolite Arts Studio Residency offers one year of free Miami Beach studio space, professional development, exhibitions, and career support, plus eligible South Florida artists receive a $15,000 housing stipend. Learn more at the website. Deadline is July 31.

The Oolite Arts Cinematic Residency supports South Florida filmmakers creating first feature films with $50,000 funding, mentorship, studio space, production resources, and industry connections for ambitious microbudget cinema. More information at the website. Deadline is July 31.

Praxis Center keeps tabs on opportunities around the art world, bringing you highlights every week and offering support, resources, and expertise to help you reach your career goals. The bad news is that rejection is inevitable when you apply for various opportunities, but the good news is that’s no reason to stop trying. If you keep your focus and make a plan, you will move forward. We have seen it time and time again.

item.title: What’s That You’re Carrying?
item.dc:creator: Brainard Carey
item.description: “People have a hard time letting go of their suffering. Out of a fear of the unknown, they prefer suffering that is familiar.” –Thich Nhat Hanh Have you ever stepped back and realized that you have been holding on tight to something that isn’t serving you? Perhaps it’s a grudge, or some small moment that […]
item.content:encoded:
“People have a hard time letting go of their suffering. Out of a fear of the unknown, they prefer suffering that is familiar.” –Thich Nhat Hanh

Have you ever stepped back and realized that you have been holding on tight to something that isn’t serving you? Perhaps it’s a grudge, or some small moment that disturbed the surface of your well-being and which, for reasons that aren’t always clear, you have been struggling to let go of. This is a common situation to find yourself in as a human being – often we become so used to operating in a space even if it’s uncomfortable that we would rather opt for the familiarity of the struggle than what might be on the other side of it.

Soumya Netrabile joined us in 2024 to talk about her show, Holding Current, which ran until October 19 of that year at Rachel Uffner Gallery. One of the drivers of the process behind the paintings in the show was Netrabile engaging with the forest. This led her to examine what attention means and how we use it, a concept that connects to her meditation practice. Holding current is a phrase in circuit theory that reflects the minimum charge required to keep a circuit in the on position. In much the same way, the work speaks to how much focus Netrabile can hold while she paints. To learn more, listen to the complete interview.

Adam Simon chatted with us around the same time about his show, Great Figures, which ran at OSMOS. The title of the show was suggested by the gallerists, and Simon agreed to its efficacy. Though he told us that he might have titled the show Fragments, a nod to the works being made up of fragments of his older pieces. That said, the imagery he used came from multiple places but all held significance to the source imagery he tapped into. To learn more about the show and Adam’s work, listen to the complete interview.

A Few Words to Keep in Your Pocket.

Consider what you may be clinging to that should have been let go of ages ago.

Outings.
